prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1485; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a rear-end collision in a parking lot involving the vehicle named on the policy. The claimant reported knee pain and said she was seated in the other vehicle at the time of impact.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone to take her statement. She described the impact the same way she did during initial intake and said she had been stopped with her foot on the brake.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the damage observed by the responding officer. No independent witnesses to the impact itself were identified.

Entry 4: Reviewed photos submitted by both parties. They confirm the general position of the vehicles and the location of the damage, though some details cannot be verified from the images alone.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle damage. The pattern and height of the damage match the impact described in the statement and the police report. A few old scratches near the bumper may predate this collision and were noted separately.

Entry 6: Confirmed coverage was in force at the time of loss and found nothing suggesting the damage occurred before the policy started. The driver is listed on the policy as a named insured.

Entry 7: Received medical records. The knee injury is consistent in kind and force with the mechanism of this collision. Records also show a minor strain to the same area many years ago that healed fully without ongoing complaints.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits tapering as the claimant's range of motion and pain improved. The provider's notes describe steady progress with no new complaints recorded in later visits.

Entry 9: Reviewed the file as a whole. The claimant's account has remained consistent across all contacts, and the documented injury and vehicle damage align with the reported impact. Moving the claim to the evaluation stage.
